voz.estilo: Speak in American English like a gripping documentary narrator revealing a classified file. Serious and a little mysterious, but at a brisk, energetic pace with short pauses.

frases: Summer 1947. A New Mexico rancher, W. W. Brazel, finds debris scattered across his land.
Rubber strips, tinfoil, tough paper and sticks.
He takes it to the sheriff. The Army at Roswell calls it a flying disc.
Major Jesse Marcel poses with the debris.
Then the story changes. Officials say it's a radar target.
Brazel told the paper: if he ever found anything else, short of a bomb, he wasn't saying a word.
videos.caption: The rancher who found the Roswell debris in 1947, in his own words. #roswell #ufo #history #declassified #mystery

frases: In 1994, the Air Force said Roswell was Project Mogul.
A secret train of weather balloons over six hundred feet long, built to detect Soviet nuclear tests.
Charles Moore launched it on June 4, 1947.
But what about the alien bodies?
Those stories first appeared in the late 1970s. More than thirty years later.
In 1997, the Air Force said witnesses were remembering test dummies dropped from balloons in the 1950s.
videos.caption: The Air Force's official answer to Roswell: Project Mogul and crash test dummies. Do you buy it? #roswell #ufo #airforce #declassified #history
